sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate Powder

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA), including the Investment Agreement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (President's Order No. 55, effective 1 January 2007, as amended by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (Order No. 3 of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Market Entity Registration (SAMR Order No. 59); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 28 December 2023, effective 1 July 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry, Government of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: obtain the official original or certified copy from the Companies Registry, have it notarized by a Hong Kong notary public if the receiving PRC authority requires signature certification, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the High Court of Hong Kong SAR. Consular legalization is not applicable and must never be chained for Hong Kong-origin documents because Hong Kong SAR is covered by the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Continued Registration) of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry, Government of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: obtain the Certificate of Good Standing directly from the Companies Registry, have it certified by a Hong Kong notary public if required, then obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong SAR. Do not sequentially attach consular legalization because Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Hong Kong investing company authorizing the establishment of the PRC WFOE and granting a Power of Attorney to authorized representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong investing company (certified by a Hong Kong notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: the signed board resolution and power of attorney must be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public to authenticate the signatures, then the notarized instrument must receive an Apostille certificate issued by the High Court of Hong Kong SAR. Consular legalization is not used in this path and no consular step may be added after the Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (and Memorandum of Association, if applicable) of the Hong Kong investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong investing company (registered with Companies Registry, Government of Hong Kong SAR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: have the Articles of Association certified as a true copy by a Hong Kong notary public, then submit the certified copy to the High Court of Hong Kong SAR for an Apostille certificate. Consular legalization is never a substitute for or a sequential supplement to this path in an Apostille Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by a licensed Hong Kong bank confirming account relationship, transactional history, and good conduct of the investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path only: the bank officer's signature must be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, and the notarized letter must then receive an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong SAR. No consular legalization is required for use in PRC filing, and the two authentication methods must remain parallel alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before name clearance or issuance of any notarization, every ultimate beneficial owner, director, shareholder, and authorized signatory of the Hong Kong investing company and the proposed PRC WFOE must be screened in real time against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, HM Treasury consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and China's domestic export-control and unreliable-entity lists. Enhanced due diligence must be performed for all politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, using independent adverse-media screening, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and residual-risk scoring. All negative hits require escalation to the compliance committee and, absent a lawful and documented exemption, rejection of the formation mandate. Screening evidence must be time-stamped, reason-tagged, and archived for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration and Reservation System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under SAMR Order No. 59 and the Administrative Measures for Enterprise Name Registration, the proposed WFOE name must adhere to the four-tier Chinese naming convention: (1) administrative division, (2) unique trade name, (3) industry description 'lithium battery materials' or 'trading' (as approved under the business scope), and (4) organization form 'limited liability company' (rendered as 'Co., Ltd.' in English). The registered name must be in simplified Chinese characters; Arabic numerals may be used only if customary and not misleading. Any foreign-language name is a separate unregistered transliteration that must be phonetically consistent with the Chinese trade name and may not appear as the authoritative registered name. The English rendition must accurately reflect the Chinese name to avoid a name mismatch during bank account opening and customs licensing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name reservation is rejected, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection decision with the reason and the applicable legal basis. Within 15 days of service, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the market supervision authority at the next higher level, or initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court. The SOP requires preserving the original application and the SAMR rejection stamp, preparing a corrected four-tier name proposal that remediates the cited conflict, and simultaneously submitting a fresh name reservation application to protect the 30-day window. Counsel should not wait for the appeal outcome before re-f

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 5, 8, 9, 10, 23, 24, 26, 27, 29, 34, 42, 45 and 46; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 4, 8, 10 and 28; Regulations on Implementing the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020); and Measures for the Administration of Registration of Market Entities (2021), Articles 8, 12, 18, 22 and 30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation through the local Administration for Market Regulation at the municipal or district level where the company's registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Company, together with the Articles of Association, the shareholder appointment instruments and the director and supervisor appointment forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: there is no statutory minimum registered capital for an ordinary wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited-liability company. The shareholder determines the registered capital and payment schedule in the Articles of Association. Under the 2023 Company Law, subscribed capital must be fully paid within five years from incorporation unless a shorter period is specified in the Articles of Association. No blocked escrow account is required by law; however, the paid-in capital must be deposited into a dedicated capital contribution account in the company's name at a bank licensed in the People's Republic of China and must be used for lawful business purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD. WHEREAS the Company is being incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the laws of the People's Republic of China, wholly owned by [Shareholder]; WHEREAS the sole shareholder has executed the Articles of Association and the Application for Registration of Establishment; and WHEREAS the first Board of Directors is empowered under the Company Law and the Articles of Association to organise the Company's statutory affairs. NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors, acting as the first governing body, HEREBY RESOLVES as follows: 1. Adoption of Articles. The Articles of Association as filed and approved by the Administration for Market Regulation are adopted as the constitution of the Company, and all directors and officers shall observe and perform their duties in accordance therewith. 2. Share Capital Subscription. The entire authorised and issued share capital of the Company is fixed at [registered capital amount], divided into ordinary shares of [par value] each, and such shares are subscribed in full by the sole shareholder on the terms recorded in the Contribution Schedule. The Board records that the shareholder's written subscription is irrevocable and constitutes an enforceable obligation to pay the capital contribution in accordance with the schedule. 3. Payment of Capital. The legal representative is authorised to open a capital contribution deposit account in the Company's name at a bank licensed in the People's Republic of China and to receive and confirm payment of the subscribed capital. The Board directs that no part of the paid-in capital be released to any other account until the bank confirmation and capital contribution verification procedures are completed. 4. Banking Authorization. The following banks are authorised as bankers of the Company: [Bank Name], [Branch], and any branch or sub-branch appointed by the legal representative. The Board authorises the bankers to honour cheques, SWIFT messages, letters of credit, wire transfers and electronic payment orders bearing the signature of the legal representative or other jointly authorised signatories, subject to the account mandate forms filed with each bank. 5. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [address], and the legal representative is authorised to execute, register and maintain the lease, utility and property management documents relating to that office. All statutory notices shall be sent to that address. 6. Appointment of Officers. The following persons are appointed as statutory officers: [Director] as Executive Director, [General Manager] as the principal operating officer, [Supervisor] as the supervisor with audit and supervisory powers, and [Legal Representative] as the legal representative of the Company. Each officer accepts the appointment and the Company shall file the required appointment instruments with the Administration for Market Regulation. 7. General Powers. The Board delegates to the legal representative, the general manager and the other officers the power to execute all declarations, tax registrations, social insurance registrations, customs registrations, bank forms, contracts and other documents reasonably necessary to complete the incorporation, registration, licensing and opening of operations; to affix the company seal; and to retain professional advisers. All acts performed pursuant to this resolution are hereby ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise name pre-approval and corporate name screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation online name reservation system / National Enterprise Name Registration System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed enterprise name through the local Administration for Market Regulation online registration platform or the national enterprise name registration system. The applicant must select the correct administrative division, trade name, industry descriptor and legal form suffix 'Limited Company'. The system will screen the name for duplication, prohibited characters and misleading similarity to existing registered names and trademarks. After preliminary approval, the name reservation notice is valid for six months. If a physical counter application is necessary, an authorised representative must present the required identity documents and the signed power of attorney. This step may be combined with establishment registration in cities implementing integrated one-window processing.
required_dossiers: Identification document of the legal representative
Power of attorney to the formation agent
Proposed Chinese trade name and English trade name declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or suspended, the applicant must select a replacement name or amend the trade name descriptor and resubmit through the same portal. Administrative review may be requested in writing, but in practice a revised name submission is faster and will not restart the statutory time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and legalization of Hong Kong shareholder documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Notary Public, Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporate documents of the Hong Kong shareholder must be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public. The notary certificate must state that each document is a true copy of the registered company records and must identify the individuals who executed the corporate resolutions. The certified package must then be legalized through the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR or transmitted by the China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited, depending on the requirement of the local Administration for Market Regulation. Once legalized, the package must be translated into Chinese for filing purposes, and the English notarized version may be submitted with a translation undertaking where the local registry permits dual-language filings.
required_dossiers: Hong Kong Memorandum and Articles of Association
Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization certificate
Power of attorney executed by the Hong Kong shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarization or legalization package is returned for deficiency, the formation agent must obtain an amended notary certificate or re-submit the package to the legalization office. If the translated text is queried, a sworn translation certificate or a revision sheet may be filed without prolonging the corporate registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of establishment registration to the Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District-level or city-level Administration for Market Regulation integrated enterprise registration hall.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment registration package at the competent Administration for Market Regulation window or through the integrated online service. The application must be executed by the sole shareholder or its authorised representative, and the legal representative must sign the relevant appointment instruments. The registry will examine the Articles of Association for mandatory provisions, verify the registered address against the lease documentation and property ownership certificate, and check the identity and eligibility of the director, supervisor and legal representative. If the documents are complete, the registry issues the Business License with a Uniform Social Credit Code and publishes the incorporation entry on the national enterprise credit information system. The issue of the Business License is the effective act of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder
Legalized and translated Hong Kong shareholder qualification documents
Property ownership certificate or landlord consent letter
Appointment letter of the legal representative
Appointment letter of the director and supervisor
Identification documents of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, the formation agent must obtain a written deficiency notice, correct the identified items within fifteen working days and resubmit the amended package. If the registry makes a substantive refusal, the applicant may request an administrative reconsideration within sixty days or file a new application after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company seal creation, bank account opening and capital contribution deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraving units, a licensed commercial bank in the People's Republic of China, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange acting through the receiving bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Business License, the company must arrange for the official company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and invoice seal to be engraved by a Public Security Bureau authorized seal engraver and complete the seal registration card. The legal representative must then open a basic deposit account and, where foreign capital will be injected, a foreign exchange capital account at a licensed commercial bank. The bank will conduct customer due diligence, may require a beneficial ownership declaration, and may ask for the source of funds of the Hong Kong shareholder. The paid-in capital must be deposited into the dedicated capital contribution account in RMB or foreign currency. The bank will handle the foreign direct investment information registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and funds may be settled only for lawful business expenditures within the approved scope.
required_dossiers: Identification document of the legal representative
Foreign direct investment information registration form prepared by the bank
Lease agreement and utility bill for the registered office
Source of funds declaration and bank statements of the shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application or imposes enhanced due diligence conditions, the company must provide the requested corporate organograms, ultimate beneficial ownership details, transaction contracts and source-of-funds evidence. If the State Administration of Foreign Exchange query arises, the bank will file a corrective filing or the company may appoint a new account bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, social insurance registration and statistical registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration e-tax platform, Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau portal, and National Bureau of Statistics local statistical office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative or financial officer must complete tax registration through the State Taxation Administration e-tax system, selecting the appropriate value-added tax payer status, corporate income tax, stamp duty and payroll-related taxes. The company must also register with the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for social insurance and housing fund contributions and complete basic statistical registration with the local statistics bureau. The tax authority will issue a taxpayer identification number identical to the Uniform Social Credit Code. Electronic invoicing may be activated after the tax authority approves the applicant's financial software and tax control equipment application. The company should also file for value-added tax invoice issuance limits and determine whether it qualifies as a general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer.
required_dossiers: Lease contract for the registered office
Identification documents of the legal representative and financial officer
Company financial seal and legal representative seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority flags the address, bank details or taxpayer status, the company must submit a corrected lease, a bank confirmation letter or a revised taxpayer status application. If social insurance registration is queried, the issue is usually cured by correcting the payroll records and employment contract dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs and foreign trade operator registration for cross-border procurement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce through the Chinese International Trade Single Window, and the customs office of the People's Republic of China through the e-port system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: To conduct cross-border procurement and trading, the company must register as a foreign trade operator under the Foreign Trade Law of the People's Republic of China and the Measures for the Registration of Foreign Trade Operators. The application is filed on the Chinese International Trade Single Window, after which the customs office issues the customs registration certificate. The company should also apply for the electronic port IC card required for customs declarations and for export tax refund handling if exports are anticipated. Should the company later handle goods subject to export or import control, an additional license from the Ministry of Commerce would be required. This step confirms that no sector-specific operating license applies to ISIC 4662 wholesale distribution of battery-grade lithium carbonate.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of the legal representative
Lease agreement for the registered office
Electronic port IC card application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Single Window application is rejected or suspended, the company must verify the Uniform Social Credit Code, ensure the legal representative has a valid electronic signature certificate and resubmit the corrected application. If the customs office requires further supporting evidence, the company must provide purchase and sale contracts, classification advice and hazardous materials declarations as appropriate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable: the registered business is pure wholesale procurement and trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder under ISIC 4662, with no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly or warehousing activity. If a physical warehouse or chemical storage site is later established, the local Municipal Emergency Management Bureau and Ecology and Environment Bureau would become competent.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable: no industrial or manufacturing operating license is required for wholesale distribution and cross-border procurement of battery-grade lithium carbonate. A foreign trade operator registration and customs registration are administrative trade qualifications, not industrial operating licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable: if warehousing or chemical storage is added, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment through the provincial Ecology and Environment Department would review the activity under the Classified Management List of Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects (2021).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable: no Environmental Impact Assessment registration, environmental impact report or environmental registration record is required for an office-based wholesale and procurement activity that does not involve construction projects, industrial installations, chemical reactions or fixed storage tanks.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable: the activity generates no process wastewater, no VOC emissions and no hazardous waste in the ordinary course of trading. Office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge standards; any waste packaging from sampled materials must be managed under general solid waste rules. If lithium carbonate is later stored in bulk, the operator must maintain a material safety data sheet and comply with the General Rules for Storage of Chemical Products but no hazardous chemical permit is triggered because lithium carbonate is not listed in the PRC Hazardous Chemicals Catalogue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the registered office-based wholesale and procurement operation. The office space must nevertheless comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China through a simple fire safety inspection by the local Fire and Rescue Section covering emergency exits, fire extinguishers and electrical safety. If a warehouse is subsequently operated, the company must obtain the Fire Safety Acceptance Certificate, complete fire control design review, arrange Civil Defense protected area approval where applicable, and conduct occupational hazard factors testing under the Work Safety Law before commencing storage operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax platform) and the STA-controlled digital tax control system for VAT invoice issuance and export rebate filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The foreign parent entity must provide notarized and apostilled constitutional documents, board resolutions, and a certificate of tax residence from its home jurisdiction. Step 2: The Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is first incorporated with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtains the business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 3: Within 30 days of obtaining the business license, the WFOE must complete tax registration through the Electronic Tax Bureau or the competent local STA office. The USCC is automatically recognized as the taxpayer identification number (TIN) for enterprise income tax, VAT, and consolidated tax returns. Step 4: The WFOE must register its bank account details, accounting system, legal representative, and finance officer in the STA taxpayer profile, and must apply for the applicable VAT taxpayer qualification based on projected turnover. Step 5: The WFOE applies for general VAT taxpayer status if its annual taxable sales exceed the statutory threshold or if such status is necessary to claim input VAT credits and export zero-rating. Step 6: The WFOE must activate electronic invoicing via the STA e-invoice platform, obtain the tax-control digital certificate or UKey, and complete the fiscal registration required before issuing Special VAT Invoices. Step 7: If a foreign non-resident entity receives Chinese-source income and has no permanent establishment in China, it does not undergo ordinary VAT registration; instead, it is registered for withholding tax purposes and is identified by its home-country TIN, while the WFOE as payer performs withholding and reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election. The WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese tax-resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law and is subject to entity-level taxation on worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available as domestic elections; any hybrid instrument or entity classification outcome is governed by the CIT regulations, special tax adjustment rules, and applicable double tax treaty provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration. All entities, regardless of turnover, must complete tax registration within 30 days of business license issuance. Below the threshold, the WFOE may remain a small-scale taxpayer unless it elects general taxpayer status to claim input VAT credits and export zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the issuance of VAT invoices through the STA-controlled digital system, including the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (e-invoice) regime and the Golden Tax IV platform. Special VAT invoices must be transmitted to the STA in near real time through authorized e-invoice service platforms or tax-control UKey devices. The STA automatically validates taxpayer identifiers, commodity/service codes, tax rates, invoice amounts, and anti-fraud digital fiscal seals. Cross-checking against VAT returns and customs export data is performed electronically. Paper invoices may remain in parallel for limited legacy scenarios, but the digital e-invoice is the standard clearance mechanism for new commercial transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Chinese VAT general taxpayer may apply the 0% export VAT rate and claim export tax rebate for battery-grade lithium carbonate sold to an overseas customer provided the goods are lawfully exported from mainland China through Chinese customs to a destination outside mainland China, including Hong Kong SAR as a separate customs territory. The sale must be between non-associated parties or at arm's length if between related parties. The exporter must receive the export proceeds in foreign currency or RMB through approved banking channels within the statutory repatriation period, retain the customs export declaration and transport documentation, and match the VAT invoice, customs declaration, logistics receipts, and FX collection records for tax authority risk control.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Customs Declaration, equivalent statutory export bill of entry)
Bill of Lading or other transport document evidencing physical movement of the goods from China to the overseas destination
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list
Bank foreign exchange collection voucher, Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), or SAFE export proceeds collection verification record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and customs authorities perform cross-agency risk matching of export declarations, VAT invoices, logistics documents, and foreign exchange collection records. Any false declaration, counterfeit bill of lading, non-delivery of goods, circular financing, artificial related-party transaction, or failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory deadline triggers retrospective cancellation of the 0% VAT rate, mandatory output VAT re-assessment, recovery of any VAT refund already received, daily late-payment surcharge, administrative penalties ranging from 50% to 500% of the evaded VAT, suspension or permanent disqualification from export tax rebate filing, and potential criminal liability for fraudulent export VAT rebate under Chinese law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) for the mainland WFOE, with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the offshore regulatory authority for the Hong Kong SAR treasury parent and the CNH market
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese Renminbi is freely convertible for current account transactions under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, including cross-border trade settlement and dividend distribution, but the capital account remains heavily controlled by SAFE. A CN WFOE importing lithium carbonate must settle payments through a designated domestic bank after submitting the trade contract, commercial invoice, customs declaration and transport documents, while all FDI equity injections from the Hong Kong parent require prior SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration and must be credited strictly to a restricted capital escrow account. Export proceeds must be repatriated to an onshore FX settlement account within the statutory period, although no mandatory conversion ratio is imposed. Dividend remittance to the Hong Kong parent, although classified as a current account remittance, is de facto reviewed by the bank against the audited annual financial statements, corporate income tax clearance certificates, retained earnings reconciliation and board resolutions, and any conversion of working capital or cross-border lending without a real trade background is prohibited. Delays of five to ten business days are common for profit repatriation because the bank and SAFE must verify tax payment, capital verification and authenticity of the underlying commercial flows, and the WFOE cannot freely convert surplus RMB into offshore currencies without an underlying genuine need.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into the WFOE's onshore foreign exchange settlement account within 90 days of the export customs declaration date, or within 30 days where payment was received in advance; the exporter may retain the proceeds in a supervised FX settlement account or convert them into RMB at the prevailing market rate through the designated Tier-1 bank, and no mandatory conversion ratio is applied, but any offshore retention beyond the approved time limit requires an SAFE exemption filing and is subject to administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account with Import/Export Sub-Ledgers
Integrated Cross-Border Trade Finance Account with LC Ancillary Facility
Cross-Border Product Account for USD/RMB Trade Clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally barred for the mainland-incorporated WFOE. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Airwallex or Revolut are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to maintain the mandatory capital escrow account, RMB basic deposit account or foreign exchange settlement account of a Chinese legal entity, and any attempt to route WFOE trade settlements through such providers violates China's foreign exchange administration rules. These EMIs may serve the Hong Kong treasury parent for CNH balances and offshore receivables only, but every onshore capital injection, import payment, export repatriation and profit remittance of the CN WFOE must clear through a licensed domestic designated foreign exchange bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch appearance is generally mandatory for the statutory legal representative and the authorised financial signatory of the WFOE when opening the RMB basic deposit account and the foreign exchange capital account. The compliance interview requires physical presentation of the Business License, Articles of Association, SAFE FDI registration certificate, tax registration certificate, corporate seal and valid passports; a non-resident legal representative may delegate an onshore director or finance officer through a notarized and legalized Power of Attorney, after which the bank still conducts a live recorded video interview with the legal representative. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted only in limited cases for the capital account at affiliated branches of the same banking group, while the basic operational RMB account always requires the original corporate seal and a face-to-face bank officer interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity where the Hong Kong parent holds the WFOE through nominee layers or a multi-tiered offshore shell structure, causing the UBO disclosure to fail the 25 percent threshold and blocking economic substance assessment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized Beneficial Ownership declaration mapping every intermediate holding entity to the individual ultimate controllers, supported by the Hong Kong parent's Certificate of Incorporation, NAR1 Annual Return, shareholder register, memorandum and articles, along with passport copies, residential address proofs, source-of-wealth statements and the WFOE board resolution naming the authorized banking signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media hits on lithium carbonate suppliers, vessels, ports or freight forwarders, particularly for cargo originating in or trans-shipping through OFAC, EU or UN restricted jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A vendor screening report from Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check or the bank's native engine confirming a no-match result for every counterparty, vessel IMO number and port; the full commercial contract with INCOTERMS and routing schedule; a non-re-export and end-use covenant; original Certificate of Origin and Bill of Lading; and ICP-MS or XRF laboratory certificates proving battery-grade purity and lawful provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering suspicion generated by import invoicing that deviates by more than 15 percent from the lithium carbonate spot benchmark, indicating potential over-invoicing, round-tripping or capital flight
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group transfer pricing documentation containing an arm's-length comparability analysis and a pricing formula linked to Fastmarkets and S&P Global Platts lithium carbonate benchmark assessments; audited financial statements of the WFOE; customs import declarations and VAT payment vouchers; a monthly benchmark-to-invoice reconciliation; and the executed contract pages evidencing volume, price adjustment and settlement mechanics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use and diversion risk triggered by the medium-risk rating of battery metals, where the bank requires proof that lithium carbonate will not be redirected to sanctioned military, defense or unauthorized industrial end-users
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An end-user certificate issued and stamped by the ultimate EV or energy storage battery manufacturer; downstream purchase orders and delivery receipts; a contractual clause prohibiting resale to defense, military or OFAC-sanctioned entities; batch-level warehouse movement and inventory ledgers; and the WFOE's internal export control policy and staff training records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital from the Hong Kong parent is transmitted by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the WFOE's Foreign Exchange Capital Escrow Account at the designated Tier-1 onshore bank, quoting the SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate number, the FDI transaction purpose code for establishing a new onshore foreign-invested enterprise and the Hong Kong parent's board resolution. The receiving bank verifies the economic substance of the capital contribution, retains the correspondent-bank advice, and triggers the statutory capital verification carried out by a licensed Chinese certified public accountant; the resulting capital verification report is then filed with the State Administration for Market Regulation. Converted RMB proceeds are released only to settle verified operating expenses within the registered business scope and cannot be used for equity investment, entrusted loans, securities trading or non-operating property purchases without prior SAFE approval, and the bank applies the negative-list screening to every disbursement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The WFOE's import settlements for battery-grade lithium carbonate are cleared through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer supported by the import contract, commercial invoice, customs declaration, transport documents and the applicable SAFE current-account trade purpose code, or preferably through an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the onshore bank and advised through a Hong Kong correspondent bank under UCP600, with payment released against compliant negotiation documents. Documentary collections under D/P or D/A terms are used only for low-value, repeated and high-trust counterparties and instructed via MT400/MT202 over the same correspondent corridors; every outbound remittance is archived in the bank's cross-border receipts and payments ledger for at least five years and must reconcile with the goods customs records and the WFOE's inventory ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY deliverable FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months concluded against verified import or export invoices under SAFE real-need doctrine
Offshore CNH/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the Hong Kong treasury parent under ISDA agreements to hedge the group's repatriation and working capital exposure

USD/CNY cross-currency swap executed by the WFOE with the domestic designated bank to convert the FDI equity injection into long-term RMB funding while respecting the SAFE registered external debt and capital quotas
SAFE-approved FX option and range accrual structures limited to the exact notional of underlying trade flows and strictly prohibited from creating open speculative positions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) - confirmation of registered office, members, directors, company secretary, and share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation, annually, by e-filing or delivery of the signed authenticated copy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On-time fee is HKD 105. If delivered after the 42-day window, additional late fees apply: HKD 870 for up to 3 months late, HKD 1,740 for 3-6 months late, HKD 2,610 for 6-9 months late, and HKD 3,480 for over 9 months late. Prosecution exposure applies to the company and every responsible officer, with fines up to HKD 50,000 and continuing daily default fines up to HKD 1,000. Repeated annual return default is a recognized trigger for administrative strike-off under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), leading to dissolution and loss of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal (BR renewal demand and payment, including levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date of the current one-year Business Registration Certificate; renewal demand is issued approximately one month before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew the Business Registration Certificate is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), subject to a maximum fine of HKD 5,000 and possible imprisonment for continuing default. Outstanding renewal fees and levies may be recovered by the Government, and the business registration may be treated as absent or suspended until payment is brought current.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) with supporting audited financial statements, tax computation, and requisite schedules such as stock listings and aged trade debtor/creditor analyses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Profits Tax Division, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of BIR51. If no return is issued and chargeable profits arise, written notification of chargeability must be given to the IRD within four months after the end of the basis period. Extended deadlines may be available on application by an authorised tax representative based on the accounting year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The IRD may raise estimated assessments under section 59(3) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), impose penalty tax up to three times the amount of undercharged tax, and prosecute the company and responsible officers for failures to file or for making incorrect returns. Continuing non-compliance attracts daily default penalties and stricter enforcement action, including distraint and court proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (BIR56A) with Forms IR56B, IR56E, IR56F, and IR56G for employee compensation, new employee notifications, and employee cessation particulars (if any employees are engaged)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Employer's Returns Office, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the date of issue of the employer's return, generally issued in respect of each year of assessment and due by the specified date on the return. Notification of commencing employment is due within 14 days; notification of cessation of employment is due within 14 days after cessation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Employers failing to file complete and timely returns without reasonable excuse are liable to fines up to HKD 10,000 per missed form and may be prosecuted by the IRD. False statements or misuse of the return may attract substantially higher fines and penalty tax. Repeated non-filing may also cause the IRD to raise estimated assessments against the employer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount audit exemption exists for an incorporated private company in Hong Kong SAR. Every company incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) must prepare annual financial statements and have those financial statements audited by a certified public accountant holding a practising certificate, unless the company has obtained dormant-company status from the Registrar and has not had significant accounting transactions during the relevant period. A dormant Hong Kong company may apply for non-audit treatment, but any resumption of trading or significant transactions immediately re-triggers the audit obligation. Large private companies, non-private companies, and companies required to prepare consolidated group accounts are also subject to additional mandatory audit, disclosure, and filing requirements. In addition, the Inland Revenue Department requires audited financial statements and tax computations in support of the annual Profits Tax Return for active companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) fully converged with IFRS; qualified private companies may adopt the Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standard for Private Entities (HKFRS for Private Entities) or the SME Financial Reporting Framework, subject to eligibility conditions. The statutory framework is supplemented by the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual UBO form to be filed with the Companies Registry. Instead, every covered Hong Kong company is required to maintain a Register of Significant Controllers (RSC) at its registered office and must record changes in significant control within 7 days of the company becoming aware of the change. Annual confirmation of members and share capital is effected through the Annual Return (Form NAR1), which must disclose current members, directors, company secretaries, registered office address, and issued shares. Transfers of shares must be evidenced by an instrument of transfer, the instrument must be presented to the Inland Revenue Department for stamping within 30 days after execution, and the Register of Members must be updated promptly to reflect the transfer. Failure to maintain or update the RSC exposes the company and every responsible person to criminal penalties, including fines of up to HKD 25,000 per contravention and continuing daily default fines for ongoing failure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Chief Executives
Minute Book of general meetings and written resolutions of members

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,400 per annum depending on the selected corporate service provider, registered office address, e-filing support, and secretarial compliance calendar management
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800 - 5,500 per annum for a Hong Kong private procurement/trading company with moderate cross-border transaction volume, including bank confirmations, inventory and receivable/ payable verification, tax computation, and certified auditor reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard CIT is 25%. No automatic location-based tax holiday exists for ordinary trading WFOEs. A small low-profit enterprise with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million, employees not exceeding 300, and total assets not exceeding RMB 50 million may qualify for a reduced 20% rate producing an effective 5% tax rate on qualifying income through 2027. A High and New Technology Enterprise may use 15%, and eligible R&D expenses enjoy an additional 100% deduction; qualifying technology transfer income may be exempt or taxed at 50% of the 25% rate, but a battery-grade lithium carbonate arbitrage and trading WFOE must prove legal and operational qualification before relying on any of these incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return of the People's Republic of China (A-type, Form A100000) with supporting schedules, including the Related Party Transactions Reporting Form and the Non-Resident Enterprise Withholding Report; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax) or a duly authorized tax clearance agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement with quarterly provisional prepayments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return is due on or before 31 May following the fiscal year ending 31 December. Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments are due within 15 days after the close of each quarter ending 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue and other operating income from battery-grade lithium carbonate powder procurement, testing, blending, and resale in China or for export.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter VAT-exclusive sales revenue. For a contractually documented buy-sell arbitrage WFOE, the full invoice value of lithium carbonate is reportable in Box 1. If the WFOE acts only as a commission agent for the non-resident HK principal, record only the commission income; do not offset principal remittances against revenue. Any cross-border related-party supply at a non-arm's-length price must be supported by contemporaneous CUP evidence and may be adjusted by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of main business: purchase cost of lithium carbonate, inbound logistics, storage, freight, insurance, testing, customs duties, and similar direct costs attributable to the sale.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only genuinely incurred costs supported by lawful special VAT invoices. Intercompany purchases from the HK affiliate must be priced at arm's length using a listed battery-grade lithium carbonate spot benchmark. Related-party service fees treated as technical royalties must satisfy deductibility rules; payments to a shell offshore parent with no actual function are non-deductible and must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses, finance expenses, and other period expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid by the resident WFOE to the Hong Kong parent are generally non-deductible under Article 49 of the CIT Implementation Regulations unless the parent provides actual services with evidence of cost incurrence and benefit to the WFOE. Allocate expenses attributable to non-taxable income proportionately. Related-party loan interest is limited by the 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio, and the interest rate is capped at the arm's-length rate; excess interest is added back to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit after deductions, being the pre-tax book profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Book profit does not by itself trigger non-resident dividend withholding tax. A withholding tax liability arises only on actual distributable profits approved by the shareholders or on amounts deemed distributed under anti-avoidance rules. Prepare board minutes, shareholder resolutions and profit distribution documents before remitting any dividend to Hong Kong.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: additions and subtractions that reconcile accounting profit to taxable income, including transfer pricing adjustments and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back all non-deductible expenses, penalties, excess entertainment expense, deemed dividend adjustments, and any transfer pricing adjustment ordered by the tax authority. Subtract tax-exempt dividends from qualified resident companies and apply unused losses within the 5-year carryforward window. If related-party transactions are not properly disclosed, the tax authority may apply Article 44 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law to assess taxable income by deemed computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and final CIT payable at 25%, after offsetting quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income at 25%; offset provisional prepayments; give foreign tax credit only for taxes paid abroad on China-sourced income under a valid DTA. Non-resident withholding rates are not entered in this box. The WFOE, as withholding agent, must separately withhold 10% (or 5% with DTA relief) on dividends and interest or royalties paid to the HK shareholder and file the corresponding withholding returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a notice to correct and a fine under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law of up to RMB 2,000 in ordinary cases and RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious non-compliance. Overdue tax accrues daily late-payment interest of 0.05% under Article 32. Underpayment caused by false or fraudulent returns attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under Article 63; false reporting without evasion may attract penalties under Article 64. Criminal tax fraud threshold is reached where intentionally evaded tax is relatively large, exposing responsible officers to criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment up to 7 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on distributions to non-resident enterprises, reduced to 5% under Article 10(3) of the China-Hong Kong DTA when the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong resident company holding not less than 25% of the paying company's share capital directly.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before any dividend remittance, the Hong Kong shareholder should obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department for the dividend income year, provide the China WFOE with the TRC, a beneficial ownership self-declaration, and ownership chain documentation proving the 25% direct shareholding throughout the distribution period, and submit the non-resident treaty relief application and withholding filing through the e-Tax system with full remittance documentation. The WFOE may withhold at the 5% treaty rate only if the beneficial owner has real economic substance in Hong Kong; if the claim is rejected, the full 10% statutory withholding tax must be paid, and any over-withholding may be recovered through a refund application within the limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest and royalties is 10%. Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, interest and royalties may be taxed at 7% where the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong resident and the payment has genuine business substance. Royalty payments for patents, know-how, software, trademarks and similar intellectual property include periodic payments for the use of or right to use the IP; fees for pure services that do not constitute royalties are treated as business profits and are taxable in China only if attributable to a Chinese permanent establishment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under SAT Public Notice [2016] No. 42, the Local File must be contemporaneously prepared where related-party transactions exceed: RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; and RMB 40 million for related-party services. The Master File is required where aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting obligations apply separately to multinational groups meeting the consolidated revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic substance and Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) apply at two levels. For the China WFOE, Article 47 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law and Article 120 of the CIT Implementation Regulations require real commercial substance in China; a pure pass-through entity with no procurement, logistics, quality control, staffing, warehousing, invoicing, risk assumption, or decision-making functions will not be respected. For the Hong Kong shareholder claiming treaty benefits, the Hong Kong Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require the offshore company to conduct its CIGA in Hong Kong, including board direction, management decisions, staff, and premises proportionate to the dividend income derived. Failure to satisfy either substance test allows the tax authorities to recharacterize the structure, deny DTA benefits, and assess CIT at 25% plus withholding tax at source.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Tax Treaty Abuse and Dividend WHT Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a non-operating shell with no physical office, employees, bank activity, board minutes, or CIGA in Hong Kong. The Chinese WFOE distributes the full trading profit to this shell and withholds only 5% dividend WHT under the China-Hong Kong DTA while the shell is not the genuine beneficial owner, and the arrangement exists principally to reduce the statutory 10% WHT and defer Chinese CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of the DTA reduction under the Principal Purpose Test and the beneficial ownership requirement; general anti-avoidance recharacterization under Article 47 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law and Article 120 of the CIT Implementation Regulations. The underpaid 10% WHT and CIT are collected with daily 0.05% interest, and Article 63 TCAA imposes a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who caused the WFOE to distribute to a sham shell and who submitted false beneficial ownership documentation may be held personally liable for restitution of the unpaid withholding tax and interest through corporate-veil piercing. Tax authorities may also request court-ordered exit restrictions, travel bans, and blacklisting of the responsible directors; where intentional fraud is established, Article 201 of the Criminal Law applies with imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Artificial Profit Shifting in Battery-Metal Cross-Border Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE buys battery-grade lithium carbonate from its HK affiliate at a price substantially above the arm's-length CUP benchmark, or sells to the HK affiliate below cost, zeroing out Chinese taxable profit. The taxpayer fails to prepare the Local File and Master File, omits related-party transaction disclosures, and uses an unapproved method to justify a distorted gross margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law authorizes special tax adjustment; Articles 107 to 123 of the CIT Implementation Regulations and SAT Public Notice 42/2016 impose the documentation obligations. Upon adjustment, taxable income is recomputed, underpaid CIT is payable with interest, and the false declaration may trigger Article 63 TCAA penalties of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or signed the intercompany contracts and TP documentation without a reasonable good-faith basis are exposed to civil veil-piercing for the unpaid tax and penalties. The tax authority may blacklist the entity and the directors and impose cross-border exit bans; knowing creation of fabricated transfer pricing documentation and fraudulent accounts invokes Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment up to 7 years and disqualification from corporate management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Invoicing / VAT and CIT Fraud on Lithium Carbonate Procurement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE claims fraudulent input VAT credits and inflated cost of goods sold using counterfeit or shell-supplier special VAT invoices for lithium carbonate that was never delivered. The inflated costs and false invoices are reflected in the annual CIT return, reducing taxable income to nil and enabling excessive dividend remissions to the Hong Kong shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law treats this as tax evasion with a penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax; Article 32 imposes daily 0.05% late-payment surcharge; Article 64 penalizes false filing. Criminal liability arises under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion and under Article 205 for issuance of false special VAT invoices, with cumulative imprisonment exposure and separate fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial controllers are personally liable for restitution of the fraudulent VAT credits, CIT, penalties, and legal costs. They may be subjected to asset freezing, travel bans, and cross-border blacklisting. Criminal conviction carries imprisonment up to 7 years for tax evasion and additional terms for false VAT invoice offences; upon conviction, the directors are disqualified from serving as legal representatives, directors, supervisors, or senior executives, and all unlawful gains are confiscated.
